title: Aloo Tama (Nepali potato and bamboo shoot curry)

ingredients.name: bamboo shoots (canned or fermented, drained and rinsed)
black-eyed peas or kidney beans, cooked

steps: Rinse the bamboo shoots well, squeeze them dry and chop.
Heat the oil, add the cumin seeds and fry the onion until golden, then add the ginger-garlic paste.
Stir in the tomatoes, turmeric, coriander, chilli and salt and cook until they break down.
Add the potatoes, bamboo shoots and beans with the water.
Cover and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the gravy has thickened.
Serve with rice.

title: Bagiya (Madheshi steamed rice-flour dumplings)
steps: Stir the hot water and salt into the rice flour and knead to a soft dough while still warm; cover it.
Boil the drained chana dal until just soft, drain and crush coarsely.
Heat the oil, fry the cumin, chilli and ginger for a minute, add the dal, turmeric and salt and cook until dry.
Take a small ball of dough, press it into a cup, add a spoonful of filling and seal into a half-moon or round dumpling.
Steam the dumplings for 15 to 20 minutes until firm and glossy.
Serve hot with tomato chutney or pickle.

title: Chatamari (Newar rice-flour crepe, Nepali pizza)
steps: Whisk the rice flour, water and salt into a smooth thin batter.
Fry the onion and garlic in a little oil, add the mince, cumin, turmeric and salt and cook until dry and browned, then stir in the tomato for a couple of minutes.
Heat a non-stick pan and pour a ladle of batter, swirling it into a thin round, then cook over medium heat until the underside sets.
Spread a layer of the mince topping over the crepe, drop a beaten egg over it if you like, and sprinkle with coriander.
Cover and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the egg is set and the edges crisp.
Slide onto a plate and serve hot, cut into wedges.

title: Chukauni (Palpa-style potato and yoghurt salad)
steps: Boil the potatoes in their skins until tender, cool, peel and cut into cubes.
Whisk the yoghurt with the salt until smooth.
Combine the potatoes with the onion, green chillies, coriander and ground cumin in a bowl.
Pour the yoghurt over and fold in gently.
Heat the oil with the chilli powder and sesame seeds for 20 seconds, pour over the salad and serve chilled or at room temperature.

title: Dal Bhat (Nepali lentil soup, rice and vegetable curry)

ingredients.name: yellow or mixed lentils (toor or masoor), rinsed
mixed seasonal vegetables (potato, cauliflower, greens), cut up
pickle (achar) and fried chillies to serve

steps: Simmer the lentils in the water with the turmeric until completely soft, about 25 minutes, then mash lightly and stir in the salt.
Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy.
For the tempering (jhanna), heat 1 tablespoon of ghee, fry the cumin, half the garlic and the dried chillies until they sizzle and darken, and pour it over the lentil soup.
In another pan heat the remaining ghee and fry the onion, remaining garlic and ginger until golden.
Add the tomato, coriander and a pinch of salt, then the vegetables with a splash of water, cover and cook for 15 to 20 minutes until tender.
Serve the rice on a plate with the dal in a bowl, the vegetable curry (tarkari) alongside, and pickle and chillies on the side.

title: Dhindo (Nepali thick millet or buckwheat porridge)

ingredients.name: gundruk or lentil soup, to serve

steps: Bring the water and salt to a boil in a heavy pot.
Slowly sprinkle in the flour while stirring continuously with a wooden spoon to avoid lumps.
Reduce the heat and keep pressing and turning the mass with the spoon for 8 to 10 minutes until it is thick, smooth and pulls away from the sides.
Shape into a smooth mound in a bowl or plate, with a little ghee on top if you like.
Serve hot with lentil soup, vegetable curry or gundruk soup, eating by pinching off pieces and dipping.

title: Gundruk ko Jhol (Nepali dried leafy green soup)

ingredients.name: dried gundruk (fermented leafy greens, from Asian shops)

steps: Soak the dried gundruk in warm water for 10 minutes, then squeeze out the water and chop it.
Heat the oil in a pan and fry the cumin seeds until they crackle.
Add the onion and garlic and cook until golden.
Stir in the tomatoes, turmeric, chilli and salt and cook until soft.
Add the gundruk and water and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes.
Serve hot with rice or dhindo.

title: Juju Dhau (Bhaktapur king curd)
steps: Bring the milk to a boil, then add the sugar and condensed milk and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring, until slightly reduced.
Cool until lukewarm, about 40 C.
Whisk the live yoghurt with a ladle of the warm milk, then stir it back into the pot with the cardamom.
Pour into small clay or glass pots, cover and keep somewhere warm for 8 to 10 hours until set.
Chill thoroughly and top with pistachios before serving.

title: Kwati (Nepali mixed sprouted bean soup)

ingredients.name: mixed beans (chickpeas, black-eyed peas, mung, green peas, soybeans), soaked and sprouted for 2 days

steps: Rinse the sprouted beans and boil them in the water until tender, about 30 to 40 minutes.
Heat the ghee in a small pan and fry the cumin seeds and ajwain until fragrant.
Add the onion and ginger-garlic paste and fry until golden, then add the tomato, turmeric, ground cumin, chilli and salt and cook until soft.
Pour the masala into the cooked beans and simmer for 10 minutes so the flavours blend.
Serve hot with a squeeze of lime and chopped coriander.

title: Lakhamari (Newar sweet crisp bread)
steps: Mix the flour, baking powder, cardamom and salt, then rub in the ghee until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs.
Dissolve the sugar in the warm milk and add to the flour to form a stiff dough.
Rest for 30 minutes, then roll out to 1 cm thick and cut into flat shapes or rings.
Fry in medium-hot oil over low-medium heat, turning, until crisp and golden brown all over.
Drain on paper and cool completely so they crisp up.

title: Laping (Nepali spicy mung bean jelly noodles)

ingredients.name: chilli oil or red chilli flakes

steps: Whisk the starch with 1 cup of cold water until no lumps remain, then stir in the remaining 2 cups of boiling water and the salt.
Cook the mixture over low heat, stirring constantly, until it thickens to a translucent paste.
Pour it into a flat container to a thickness of about 1.5 cm and chill for 1 to 2 hours until firm.
Mix the soy sauce, sesame oil, garlic, chilli oil, vinegar and pepper into a sauce.
Cut the jelly into wide strips and toss them with the sauce, cucumber, coriander and spring onion.
Serve it cold, straight from the fridge, as a refreshing spicy snack.

title: Momo (Nepali steamed chicken dumplings)

ingredients.name: ground Timur pepper or black pepper

steps: Mix the flour with the water and a pinch of salt into a firm dough, knead for 8 minutes and rest it covered for 30 minutes.
Combine the chicken, onion, garlic, ginger, coriander, cumin, pepper, soy sauce, oil and salt for the filling.
Roll the dough thin and cut into 8 cm circles, then put a spoonful of filling in each and pleat the edges to close.
Steam the dumplings in a lightly oiled steamer for 12 to 15 minutes until the dough is translucent and the filling is cooked.
For the sauce, roast the tomatoes, chillies and garlic until charred and blend with salt into a thick chutney.
Serve the momos hot with the tomato chutney.

title: Nepali Tea (Nepali spiced milk tea)
steps: Boil the water with the cardamom, ginger, cloves and cinnamon for 3 minutes.
Add the tea leaves and boil for 1 minute.
Pour in the milk and sugar and bring back to a boil, then simmer for 3 to 4 minutes.
Strain into cups and serve hot.

title: Sekuwa (Nepali grilled spiced meat)

ingredients.name: boneless goat or lamb, cut into bite-size pieces
sliced onion, cucumber and lime to serve

steps: Mix the oil, ginger-garlic paste, cumin, coriander, chilli, turmeric, pepper, lemon juice and salt into a marinade.
Coat the meat thoroughly and marinate for at least 2 hours, ideally overnight in the fridge.
Thread the meat onto skewers.
Grill over charcoal or under a hot grill for 15 to 20 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through with slightly charred edges.
Serve hot with sliced onions, cucumber, lime and flattened rice (chiura) or roti.

title: Sel Roti (Nepali sweet rice-flour ring bread)
steps: Mix the rice flour with the sugar, cardamom, mashed banana, melted ghee and milk, adding water gradually until you have a smooth, thick but pourable batter.
Rest the batter for 30 minutes so the flavours develop.
Heat oil about 4 cm deep in a wide pan over medium heat.
Pour or pipe a ring of batter into the oil, using a squeeze bottle or a cloth with a hole, and fry until the underside is golden.
Turn gently, fry until golden all over, then lift out and drain.
Serve warm or at room temperature with potato curry or on its own as a snack.

title: Thukpa (Himalayan noodle soup)
steps: Heat the oil in a pot and fry the onion, garlic and ginger until golden.
Add the meat and cook until it has changed colour, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomato, cumin, turmeric, chilli powder and salt and cook until the tomato is soft.
Add the stock and soy sauce, bring to a boil and simmer for 15 minutes, then add the carrot and cabbage and cook for 5 minutes more.
Boil the noodles separately until tender and divide among bowls.
Ladle the hot soup over the noodles and finish with coriander and lime juice.

title: Yomari (Newar steamed rice-flour dumpling with molasses)
steps: Stir the hot water and salt into the rice flour and knead into a soft smooth dough while still warm; cover so it does not dry out.
Mix the jaggery, coconut, sesame seeds and ghee into a sticky filling.
Pinch off lemon-sized balls of dough, flatten each in your palm into a cup, fill with the sweet mixture and close.
Shape each dumpling with a pointed top like a fig, sealing the edges firmly.
Steam for 15 to 20 minutes until the dough is glossy and set.
Serve warm; the molasses melts into a syrup inside.
